{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.

@ajs, 2026-10-22, in his words: "not sure this is a systems engineering view or a being able to break a higher level tier into smaller designs or exactly how it fits in reflow2. The concept I'm thinking about is as we've introduced: lines of reasoning, mathematical proofs, logical operations, etc, could we role them up in a decision node at a higher level. Say, in a standard reflow2 design project, we have make a decision to take path A vs path B. … say I want to augment that decision with a whole line of reasoning to support that. Could either:
1) expand that node into all the nodes and edges that make up my line of reasoning and basically swap that single node out for all the lines if reasoning node OR
2) could have a separate graph that contains the whole line of reasoning and still have the standard design graph be one node, but with a pointer to the whole line of reasoning graph.
In a systems engineering type perspective, solution 2 means that the line of reasoning is almost a component of the higher level design graph. By splitting them, could potentially allow whole other groups whose whole function is to perform that line of reasoning graph and all that is reported to the design graph is take path A versus path B."

ALREADY SETTLED (searched first; this is accepted intent, not open):
- A Decision is a NODE. Requirements are GOVERNED_BY it; an Inference can CONCLUDE it.
- req:a-choice-that-rests-on-checkable-premises-is-recorded-as-a-chain: a choice resting on checkable things is a stated step concluding the Decision, and a settled decision shows its acceptance and its chain's verdict side by side. That is his option 1, with the chain hanging UNDER the decision.
- req:reasoning-crosses-designs-within-a-hub: a premise naming a record in another design carries its truth and proof status. That is option 2's plumbing.
- req:recursive-black-box-decomposition: every element is a black box with function and interfaces, nested as deep as the design needs. That is his systems-engineering frame.
- cap:a-design-receives-a-requirement-from-another-proposed-with-its-origin: work can already be handed to another design, with its status reported to the parent.

WHAT IS OPEN, the HOW. Options in his terms:
(a) ONE DESIGN, TWO ZOOMS (his option 1, without the swap). The decision node stays the anchor. The chain stays beneath it. A read-back shows it COLLAPSED (the choice, the verdict, "rests on N steps, M contested, conditional on X") or EXPANDED (the whole line). Nothing is swapped out.
(b) THE REASONING AS ITS OWN DESIGN, A BLACK BOX OF THE PARENT (his option 2).
   - The reasoning lives in its own design, which another group may own.
   - The parent pins it (external_dependency) at a reviewed revision.
   - The parent's Decision rests on one far premise: that design's conclusion, "A over B".
   - The INTERFACE is the published conclusion, together with its reading (supported, contested, conditional, and on what). It is not the bare answer.
   - A "decide A vs B" question could be ALLOCATED to the reasoning design, the way a requirement is today. That design's owners work it, and the parent sees its status.
(c) START INLINE, EXTRACT LATER. A line begins under the decision (a). When it grows, or a different group should own it, it is moved into its own design (b) with its links kept. This is related to dec:idea-a-design-takes-a-chunk-of-another-design-and-inherits-it.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- A LITERAL SWAP (option 1 as worded) loses the anchor. Requirements are GOVERNED_BY the decision node, and reflow2 deliberately keeps "the owner accepted it" and "the chain concludes it" as two claims. Replacing the node with its reasoning merges them. Hanging beneath it keeps both. That is why (a) keeps the node.
- "ALL THAT IS REPORTED IS A VERSUS B" is the risk in (b). A bare answer hides whether it is contested, conditional, or resting on one weak premise: Tao's "answers vs insight", and the Lucas–Penrose finding that the translation premises carry the dispute. The interface must carry the verdict's quality. "Take A" with no "how sure, resting on what" is the helicopter, not the map.
- THE OWNER STILL DECIDES. A group's conclusion is a recommendation the parent's owner accepts (Anthony's line, 2026-10-17: reflow2 records, checks structure and computes; the agent proposes; the owner decides). The far verdict reads beside the acceptance, never instead of it.
- SPLITTING HAS REAL COSTS:
  - a pin can go stale;
  - the far group must share the design for its truth to be read;
  - a what-if must cross the boundary (it continues across designs today, one design at a time).
  Not every decision earns a design of its own; most should stay (a).

SIZE (a finding):
- (a) small. It is a collapsed or expanded read of what already exists, and close to Tao idea A (dec:idea-a-line-of-reasoning-is-read-back-as-an-exposition-a-person-can-follow-forward).
- (b) moderate. Much exists (cross-design premises, pins, allocation); new would be allocating a QUESTION or DECISION, not only a requirement, and a decision reading a far conclusion as its premise.
- (c) moderate to large. Moving records between designs while keeping their links.
